import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 590

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/590](https://www.erdosproblems.com/590)
 - [Ch72] Chang, C. C., A partition theorem for the complete graph on {$\omega\sp{\omega }$}. J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. A (1972), 396-452.
 - [Sp57] Specker, Ernst, Teilmengen von Mengen mit Relationen. Comment. Math. Helv. (1957), 302-314.
 - [La73] Larson, Jean A., A short proof of a partition theorem for the ordinal {$\omega \sp{\omega }$}. Ann. Math. Logic (1973/74), 129-145.
-/

open Cardinal Ordinal

namespace Erdos590

universe u

/--
Let $α$ be the infinite ordinal $\omega^{\omega}$. It was proved by Chang [Ch72] that any red/blue
colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3]
theorem erdos_590 : OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ ω) (ω ^ ω) 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Specker [Sp57] proved that when $α=ω^2$ any red/blue
colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3]
theorem erdos_590.variants.two : OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ 2) (ω ^ 2) 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Specker [Sp57] proved that when $α=ω^n$ for $3≤ n < \omega$ then it is not the case that any
red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3]
theorem erdos_590.variants.ge_three_false {n : ℕ} (h : 3 ≤ n) :
    ¬ OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ n) (ω ^ n) 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Let m be a finite cardinal $< \omega$. Let $α$ be the infinite ordinal $\omega^{\omega}$.
It was proved by Milnor that any red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a
red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$. A shorter proof was found by Larson [La73]
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3]
theorem erdos_590.variants.finite_cardinal (m : ℕ) : OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ ω) (ω ^ ω) m := by
  sorry

end Erdos590

findings.description: The docstring introduces m but still concludes with a blue K₃ (line 63). The Lean theorem correctly uses m as the blue clique's cardinality, so the prose describes only the triangle case rather than the finite-cardinal extension.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/590, third paragraph: the result remains true if we replace K₃ by K_m “for all finite m<ω.”
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “a blue $K_3$” with “a blue $K_m$” in this docstring. Keep the Lean statement unchanged.

findings.description: The docstring attributes the extension to “Milnor” (line 62), whereas the cited source attributes it to Milner. This is an attribution slip, not an error in the Lean proposition.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/590, third paragraph: “Milner modified Chang's proof” to obtain the extension to all finite m.
findings.suggested_fix: Change “Milnor” to “Milner,” preferably saying that Milner modified Chang's proof.

reformulations.difference: The shared Ramsey predicate uses two complementary simple graphs and specifies the finite blue target by cardinality instead of directly using an ordinal partition relation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: In the Boolean algebra of simple graphs, IsCompl red blue forces blue = redᶜ, so distinct unordered pairs receive exactly one color. Ordinal.ToType realizes the stated ordinal, and the subtype order used by typeLT is the inherited order required by the source. For finite m, typeLT s = m iff #s = m, by Ordinal.card_eq_nat and Ordinal.card_type. The scratch file proves the general equivalence with the single-graph formulation having a blue set of order type m. This also applies to all three variants.

reformulations.difference: The finite-cardinal parameter is represented by an unrestricted natural number, including 0, 1, and 2.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every cardinal below ℵ₀ is the cast of a natural number, and every natural-number cast is below ℵ₀. The scratch file proves the corresponding universally quantified ↔. The smallest cases are harmless: m=0 uses the empty blue clique; m=1 uses a singleton since ω^ω is nonempty; for m=2, either there is a blue edge or the whole graph is red. These boundary cases were proved independently in Lean.

Original scan: https://www.e-periodica.ch/cntmng?pid=com-001%3A1956%3A31%3A%3A16&bot=1 ; DOI 10.5169/seals-515706.

Chang [Ch72], DOI 10.1016/0097-3165(72)90105-7: Crossref bibliographic record and publisher metadata at https://api.elsevier.com/content/article/PII:0097316572901057?httpAccept=text/xml (not the full text).

Larson [La73], DOI 10.1016/0003-4843(73)90006-5: Crossref bibliographic record and publisher metadata at https://api.elsevier.com/content/article/PII:0003484373900065?httpAccept=text/xml (not the full text).

review.notes: All four Lean propositions faithfully state the cited results; only the two prose slips above were found. All research-solved tags agree with the source, which currently marks the main problem PROVED (LEAN). Scratch checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully and also verify that negating the Ramsey predicate asserts a countercoloring excluding both alternatives, that the complement hypothesis is satisfiable, and that the predicate is not identically true. Finite clique computations behaved as expected. Chang's and Larson's full texts remained inaccessible through the publisher; their stated results were checked against the cited Erdős page. Specker's relevant original statements were read directly. No repository files were edited.
